prompt:
You are a grounded brand-outreach assistant for our team. Use only the evidence passages below.
Never use outside knowledge. Return valid JSON only.

Separate three things:
1. OBSERVED FACTS - things a passage actually states about this company. Each fact is a claim with an id (C1, C2, ...),
   the passage id(s) that support it, and an exact quote copied word-for-word from that passage.
2. UNKNOWNS - things the evidence does not tell us (put them in "unknowns"). A channel, program or audience that does
   not appear in these passages is UNKNOWN. It is never a weakness, never a "gap", and never a reason for outreach.
3. PROPOSALS - collaboration ideas from our team. Proposals are not facts, but each must build on a positively supported
   fact (an existing campaign, partnership, product, community, value or theme) and cite that premise.

Rules:
- Put a claim marker like {C1} (curly braces) right after every factual statement in every field, including the
  email and Instagram idea. Do not write citation numbers yourself; markers are converted to citations later.
- A claim's "quote" must be copied character-for-character from the cited passage: 5 to 25 consecutive words, no
  paraphrasing, no joining of separate sentences. If you cannot find such a quote, drop the claim and every sentence
  that depends on it.
- Audience and strategy sentences are factual: each needs a marker. If no passage states the audience, write
  INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE instead of guessing.
- Pitch lines (email subject, hook, concept) should describe the proposed post ("A carousel featuring ...",
  "Collaborate on ..."). Any statement in them about what the company already does needs a marker.
- Respect passage types. "proposed_or_mock_work" and "author_recommendation" passages describe ideas, not things the
  company did: never state them as company activity. "provider_reported_result" passages are claims by a vendor or
  agency: attribute them ("X reports that ..."). "creator_or_influencer_audience_data" describes creators' followers,
  not the company's customers. "vendor_generated_profile_or_analytics" passages are a tool vendor's estimates
  (e.g. inferred age ranges): attribute them and never present them as the company's own data.
  "forward_looking_statement" passages describe plans or intentions, not completed activity.
- Mind time: if a passage describes past activity, do not present it as current.
- "marketing_gaps" may only contain a weakness that a passage positively states. Usually it is [].
- Never promise results. Describe benefits as goals or possibilities ("could", "aims to"), not guaranteed outcomes.
- Decision: write "draft" when at least one concrete, evidence-supported collaboration opportunity exists. Otherwise write
  "abstain", give an abstain_reason, set pitch fields to INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE and leave collaboration_opportunities empty.
- The email is from our team to the company, proposing one collaborative Instagram post. The pitch, the post idea and
  every collaboration opportunity are for Instagram only (no TikTok, YouTube, podcasts or other channels).
- When a sentence uses a vendor, agency or analytics passage, name that source in the sentence itself
  ("According to AdLibrary, ...", "Attentive reports that ...").
- Each "unknowns" item names one specific thing the passages do not tell us (e.g. "Whether X runs a creator program").
  Never write placeholder text such as "what the evidence does not show".

Required JSON:
{
  "decision": "draft" or "abstain",
  "abstain_reason": "string or empty",
  "claims": [{"id": "C1", "kind": "fact | provider_reported | premise", "statement": "string",
              "passage_ids": ["P1"], "quote": "exact words from the passage"}],
  "brand_summary": "Full sentences, each followed by its marker, e.g. "X makes ... {C1}." Never only markers. Or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "likely_target_audience": "A full sentence followed by its marker, or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "current_marketing_strategy": ["text with markers"],
  "unknowns": ["one specific open question, e.g. Whether the company works with creators"],
  "marketing_gaps": [],
  "collaboration_opportunities": ["proposal that builds on a cited fact {C2}"],
  "instagram_post_idea": {"hook": "string", "concept": "string", "why_it_fits": "string"},
  "email_subject": "string",
  "email_body": "string"
}

Company: Bombas (company_id bombas; category: socks and basics with a donation model)
Official domains: bombas.com
Recipient: the marketing team
Packet status: ok

[P4] source: https://blog.osum.com/bombas-target-market/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown

This targeted approach has played a significant role in Bombas’ success in the market."

[P5] source: https://www.projectpractical.com/bombas-marketing-strategy/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Through digital advertising, Bombas has been able to effectively reach its target audience online, driving brand awareness and driving conversions. Through partnerships with popular podcasts, they have been able to reach a highly engaged audience and effectively communicate their brand mission. This strategy has not only allowed them to forge meaningful connections with their target audience but has also served as a platform for sharing their philanthropic efforts and the impact they are making in the community."

[P6] source: https://www.projectpractical.com/bombas-marketing-strategy/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Promotion Strategy Bombas employs a diverse range of promotional tactics to create brand awareness and drive sales. They leverage social media platforms to engage with their target audience, share their mission, and highlight new product offerings. Additionally, Bombas utilizes traditional advertising channels, such as television and print media, to reach a wider audience and strengthen their brand presence. Collaborations with influencers, celebrities, and like-minded organizations further amplify their promotional efforts. By utilizing a mix of digital and traditional marketing strategies, Bombas effectively promotes their brand message to a broad and diverse audience."

[P7] source: https://www.opensend.com/post/bombas-marketing-strategy | document: third_party_confirmed | type: provider_reported_result | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Social Media Platform Strategy Bombas treats each platform distinctly: * TikTok: 56.3% of influencer content, focusing on authentic creator partnerships * Instagram: 43.7% of influencer content, blend of polished and user-generated content * YouTube: 450+ creator partnerships for longer-form storytelling The geographic distribution shows U.S. focus: 80.4% of content from U.S. creators, with 5.1% Canada and 4.2% UK."

[P8] source: https://blog.osum.com/bombas-target-market/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Targeting Strategies Bombas employs various targeting strategies to reach their intended audience: * Mission-driven Marketing: Bombas leverages their mission and philanthropic nature to connect with their target market. By emphasizing their one-for-one donation model and commitment to helping those in need, they attract consumers who value socially conscious brands. * Online Marketing: Bombas utilizes social media marketing and digital advertising to reach their target market. They engage with millennials through platforms like Instagram and Facebook, creating visually appealing content and sharing their brand story."

[P9] source: https://www.projectpractical.com/bombas-marketing-strategy/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: actual_activity | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Example of Bombas’ Test-and-Learn Approach One example of Bombas’ test-and-learn approach is their foray into influencer marketing. The company initially identified potential influencers aligned with their brand values and introduced a small-scale campaign to gauge its effectiveness. After analyzing the results and measuring the return on investment, Bombas scaled up their influencer marketing efforts, partnering with impactful influencers to reach a wider audience. By implementing these best practices, Bombas has been able to scale their marketing efforts strategically while maintaining a lean team and ensuring profitability."

[P10] source: https://www.opensend.com/post/bombas-marketing-strategy | document: third_party_confirmed | type: actual_activity | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Authentic Storytelling Around Social Contributions Purpose-driven messaging requires authenticity. Bombas varies emphasis based on context: * Donation milestone campaigns: Customers prioritize the giveback story * Performance product launches: Consumers value quality messaging over purpose * Seasonal moments: Different emphasis at different times of year The key insight from co-founder Heath: \"It's a different emphasis at different times of year\" based on what the audience needs to hear."
